page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, 4.0 GB of system memory providing 2.0 GB per core, and no local storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the lower tiers of performance. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is 1098.39, categorized as weak, while multi-core performance drops to the poor category at 1457.09. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only small block cached memory at 81.44 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 9.37 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect these constraints, yielding a single-core score of 923.0 and a multi-core score of 1096.0.

This instance offers dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent access to its processing resources without the virtualization steal time common in shared-core environments. However, the hardware relies on an older Intel Xeon processor, which limits its computational throughput. The absence of local storage requires external block storage attachment, and the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 restricts its utility for memory-intensive tasks. From a qualitative cost perspective, it represents an entry-level dedicated resource tier suitable for workloads where predictable CPU access is required but raw processing speed is not critical.

Given the benchmark profile, the ecs.sn1ne.large is suited for lightweight applications. These include basic static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 1.22 GB/sec, low-volume Redis key-value operations at 1.45 million operations per second, and small-scale software compilation. It is not suited for large-scale database operations, heavy multi-threaded processing, or modern large language model inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.large is an entry-level, compute-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM on an x86_64 architecture. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor under the KVM hypervisor, it provides a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with no local storage included. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower percentiles, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1098.39 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1096.0. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention, though the older processor architecture limits overall throughput. This instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic static web serving, small-scale Redis operations, and simple utility tasks that require dedicated but modest computational resources.
